failed_attempts.reason_failed: Both repos routinely have a local main/branch tip well ahead of origin/main from concurrent sessions. Branching from the local tip silently adopts all of it — and pushing then PUBLISHES work other sessions had not chosen to push.

failed_attempts.description: Chained `git worktree add ... ; cd <path> ; git cherry-pick <sha>` with semicolons after the worktree add failed on a config lock.

failed_attempts.reason_failed: Semicolon chaining let a failed cd fall through to commands that then ran in the wrong repository. A `git reset --hard` recovery would additionally have destroyed 18 uncommitted files belonging to other sessions.

failed_attempts.description: Used `pkill -f 'cargo test -p praxia-rig-tools'` to stop a runaway build.
failed_attempts.outcome: Exit 144 repeatedly; the target survived. The pattern matched the bash wrapper running pkill itself, so it killed its own shell.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: `pkill -f` matches the full command line including the invoking shell. Correct approach: `pgrep -x cargo`, read /proc/<pid>/cmdline, kill by PID.

failed_attempts.description: Hypothesised that plan_audit and spec_adversarial score blind because their nodes have no read tools, and was about to recommend adding ripgrep to the plan_audit registry (a Rust change plus a global cargo install).
failed_attempts.outcome: DISPROVEN by a 2x2 before recommending it. Handed gemma-4-12B the literal `0 (no matches)` probe output in-prompt, it referenced none of it and still called a non-existent flag 'a CLI check' (verification_design 4/5 -> 3/5, for an unrelated reason). qwythos-v2 with the same evidence reached 2/5 and FAIL.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: Read access is necessary but NOT sufficient — the effect is an interaction between evidence availability and backend. Even the best local arm confabulated a flag and missed two of four defects, so no backend tier makes model judgment reliable here. The fix that works is checking at the write boundary (shipped as praxia PR #62), not asking the model.

failed_attempts.description: Ran `praxia docs index` from inside a git worktree to regenerate INDEX.md after adding a spec.
failed_attempts.outcome: Dropped 28 entries (2 insertions, 40 deletions) and reverted the header to '# praxia Internal Docs', re-introducing the regression commit 08be900 had fixed. Both `docs index` and `docs check` reported success on the truncated output (`ok: true, error_count: 0`).
failed_attempts.reason_failed: bathos gitignores .praxia/ and force-adds only ~10 docs, so a worktree materialises a strict subset of the doc tree. Regeneration is only 'total and idempotent' when every indexed doc is on disk. Filed as debt #1097.

failed_attempts.description: Ran a multi-statement psql heredoc opening with BEGIN; to move debt rows between workspaces. Separately, hit `.git/config.lock` in the praxia checkout.
failed_attempts.outcome: The psql heredoc printed `UPDATE 9` but rolled back at session end because it had no COMMIT;. On the lock: unlike the prior session's diagnosis (task 260729_bathos_pr_triage, a2, which called it a sandboxed device-file stand-in), this instance was a REAL stale lock — a 0-byte regular file ~8 hours old with no git process holding it. Removing it outside the sandbox fixed config writes, verified by a write/unset round-trip.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: An open transaction is rolled back when stdin closes; the UPDATE count is not evidence of a commit — verify by re-reading the rows. And .git/config.lock has two distinct causes: a sandbox device-file stand-in (unfixable, work around) and a genuine stale lock (removable). Check size, age and `pgrep -x git` before deciding which.

failed_attempts.description: Read a rig-run flow's terminal output with `grep -E 'verdict|confidence|research_id|note:|Wrote|committed'` and concluded from the absence of a match that the recon.jsonl dual-write was undisclosed (filed as debt #1086).
failed_attempts.outcome: FALSE. The CLI does print `also: .praxia/recon.jsonl (key: recon_id = ...)`; my grep simply had no pattern for `also:`. Corrected #1086 in place and downgraded it to a record-labelling gap.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: A filter that does not match something is not evidence the thing is absent. This recurred three more times in the same session (a wrong JSONL key — `scores` vs `dimensions`; a shell-quoting-mangled `grep LIKE` returning 0 on a file that plainly contains it). failed_attempts.description: Considered wiring obligation trigger 3 (adversarial_check_fired) by guessing the polarity of when an adversarial_check 'fires'.
failed_attempts.outcome: Deliberately refused, then resolved from evidence. The D3 ADR defines the field as a condition that 'would flip the outcome if the hypothesis were wrong', and the v0.6 spec's example pairs condition='temp_std < 5' with adversarial_check='temp_std < 5 AND n_steps >= 10000 AND dt_fs <= 0.5' — a strengthened conjunct. failed_attempts.reason_failed: Guessing would have been actively harmful: new_experiment's template shipped adversarial_check = 'metric >= 5.0' against condition = 'metric < 5.0', its own negation, which under the correct polarity is a contradiction firing on EVERY passing run of every scaffolded experiment. Fixed, and lint heuristics (a)/(b) — described as shipped in the ADR since 260526 but never implemented — now catch that shape.

failed_attempts.description: Tagged the release at the version-bump commit 99da265 (considered, caught before executing).
failed_attempts.outcome: Would have run the OLD ungated publish.yml and published without any verification.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: GitHub Actions runs the workflow file FROM THE TAGGED COMMIT, not from main's tip. Tagging the release commit executes whatever publish.yml existed there. Tagged 9c6bee1 (the publish-gate commit) instead.

failed_attempts.description: Compared the git tag against `uv version --short` output without NO_COLOR.
failed_attempts.outcome: Comparison sees $'\033[36m0.13.0a2\033[39m' and never matches — would have rejected every legitimate release.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: uv emits ANSI escape codes even when stdout is a pipe rather than a TTY. Verified with od -c. Fails closed, so it would have been caught at the first tag — by blocking it.

failed_attempts.description: Read the declared version with bare `uv version --short` in a pre-build CI step.
failed_attempts.outcome: uv re-locks and syncs the project as a side effect, before the intended build step.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: `uv version` is not a pure read. --frozen makes it one. (--no-sync also works but is mutually exclusive with --frozen.)

failed_attempts.description: Polled `gh pr checks <n>` and parsed the state with awk '{print $2}'.
failed_attempts.outcome: Wait script exited immediately, reporting 'pending' as a terminal verdict.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: The check name 'test (3.13)' contains a space, so awk's default splitting makes $2 = '(3.13)', never the bucket. Use `gh pr checks <n> --json bucket --jq '.[0].bucket'` instead.

failed_attempts.description: Passed a hand-typed/short commit SHA to a background CI-wait script matching on headSha.
failed_attempts.outcome: Script never matched and would have run to timeout; had to TaskStop and restart twice.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: Guessed the full SHA instead of reading it from `git rev-parse`, and separately passed a short SHA where the API returns full ones. Always resolve with git rev-parse and match on the full value.

failed_attempts.description: Asserted archive_tool(project='') raises ValueError in a new test.
failed_attempts.outcome: Test failed: DID NOT RAISE.
failed_attempts.reason_failed: It returns {'error': 'project parameter is required'} rather than raising. My own test bug, not a code defect — read the guard clause before asserting on its shape.
